binding.statement: The audited ur/ui.chat.json is byte-identical in the read-only `git archive` export of c5e19ecec8 where every gate ran, and in the object database (`git show c5e19ecec8:src/i18n/catalogues/ur/ui.chat.json | shasum -a 256` = e71815d9b12e38a2b327a551bd105b58937a613963119edae0db169dad1b7ea6, audit.log section 9b). A later commit that changes a byte voids this record.

delta.proof: Parsed-JSON comparison over five snapshots (git show into a throw-away dir, never the shared checkout): 0 value mismatches in en and ur for all 142 keys; 0 raw-line mismatches after allowing only the JSON member separator (the last member of a file has no trailing comma), so every audited key's stored text is byte-identical to the file the earlier receipt bound. Key order in the union is exactly origin/main's 124 keys followed by wave A's 18, so the merge moved no base line; en and ur key sets and order are identical to each other; the 27 wave keys share no key name. See audits/evidence/ur/ui.chat/union-ur-20261028-fc773f54ac28/audit.log section 2.

findings.problem: The counted noun is fixed as the plural باریاں, but Urdu agrees a counted noun with the number that precedes it in the clause: 1 باری, 2 باریاں. The chip prints the noun straight after {completed}, so the first completed turn of any running loop reads 10 میں سے 1 باریاں (proved by real render, not by inspection). English reads correctly at every value because its noun agrees with of {total}. The English argument is a number and locale-parity pins the type, so no plural arm can be added to fix it here. Meaning is never in doubt and nothing unsafe follows, which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.fix_note: The classifier form this same file already uses in ui.chat.checkpoint.turn and checkpoint.jump_* (باری {turn}), grammatical at every count and still carrying both numbers. If the noun must stay a count noun, {total, number} باریوں میں سے {completed, number} keeps agreement with the total instead, which is correct for the total >= 2 a running loop reaches.

current_report_verdict.summary: The union holds together: every key is byte-identical to the audited wave or base bytes, no cross-wave term/register/punctuation collision was found, and the only defect is one count-noun agreement in the loop chip at {completed}=1 (minor, fix suggested).

observations_not_findings.topic: RTL hazard: {digits} range reverses inside the Urdu sentence
observations_not_findings.detail: ui.chat.question_dock.hint.options passes digits = 1-3 (question-dock.tsx:225-227). Rendered with real intl-messageformat and reordered by FriBidi under an RTL base direction, the line shows the range as 3-1: the hyphen is a neutral between two number runs, takes the paragraph direction, and splits the range (measured with fribidi; the shaped visual line reads ... جواب دیتا ہے 3-1 ... Enter). The catalogue text is correct and shaped like the English; the fix belongs at the call site, exactly as src/renderer/src/features/agent-hub/components/hub-skills-library.tsx:631 does it (FSI/PDI around the interpolated value, reason recorded there). Reported for the renderer lane; it does not change this catalogue verdict.

observations_not_findings.topic: RTL hazard: the pass-through {body} sentence keeps its final stop at the far left
observations_not_findings.detail: ui.chat.provider_error.headline.out_of_credits ends with {body}, the provider's own English sentence (sample: Top up to continue.). Under an RTL paragraph the final full stop is a trailing neutral that takes the paragraph direction and lands at the visual left edge, detached from the sentence (measured with fribidi). Same class and same remedy as UUR-O1; the provider sentence itself is never translated, so no catalogue wording can fix it.

observations_not_findings.topic: ASCII ellipsis in mermaid.loading mirrors the English source
observations_not_findings.detail: ui.chat.mermaid.loading is the only one of the file's five ellipsis values that uses three ASCII dots - and the English source uses three ASCII dots there too ('Loading diagram...'), while the other four are U+2026 in both files. The ur value is therefore a faithful copy, not a typography slip introduced by translation; if the programme wants one ellipsis convention it should change the English source, which will then move this key in every locale.

observations_not_findings.topic: secret, job and section vocabulary is house style, but the job row is unrecorded
observations_not_findings.detail: راز for secret is used across 4 ur files (راز کا خانہ, راز کی درخواست), so secret_answer_label (راز کا جواب) and secret_value_label (راز کی قدر) are consistent rather than novel. جابز for jobs appears in 3 ur files; the core glossary's ur cell is '-' and glossary footnote 6 says the wave that translates it records the endorsed rendering in the locale guide, while style-guides/ur.md records no job call. That is a documentation gap for the glossary/style-guide owners, not a defect in this catalogue. حصہ for a settings section matches the corpus (سیکشن appears in no ur file).

observations_not_findings.topic: the kept-English literals are the words the UI actually uses
observations_not_findings.detail: yes/no/1/2 stay Latin because a typed approval answer resolves through the shipped English word lists; Approve/Deny stay Latin because they are APPROVAL_OPTIONS' own labels (src/renderer/src/features/chat/approval-words.ts:49-50), printed on the buttons the hint names; Enter/Esc/Escape/Up/Down are physical keys. فائل کا راستہ نقل کریں, quoted inside highlights.file_resolution_failed, is byte-identical to the real control label ui.common.file_actions.copy_file_path in ur, so the instruction names a control the reader can find.

observations_not_findings.topic: no English fallback and no exemption needed
observations_not_findings.detail: No value in ur/ui.chat.json is identical to its English source (0 of 142). چیٹ (Chat tab) and خام (Raw tab) are Urdu-script renderings, so unlike es this file needs no locale-parity identical-value exemption.
